title: Father's Silver Leaf string band and the Claiborne Williams band in Donaldsonville
summary: His father George played guitar in the Silver Leaf string band in the Irish Channel until his children came; his mother came from Donaldsonville, home of Claiborne Williams's reading brass band, which Sayles remembers playing Sunday concerts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, let's go back before your time, back as far as we can, I guess. You say your father played?

Yeah, my father was one of the original men of what they call the Silver Leaf Band. It was a string band. And from what he told me, there was a man that played violin. See the name of the iPhone's? They were out in the riverfront. He played violin and sax. Do you remember him? No, I don't get it. And then he and my daddy and there was, my daddy played guitar and he on violin. And then they had a bass. And I don't remember what a bass player, but at that time, my daddy tell me they used to, all the fellas used to work in a deal, like poor jobs, different jobs, because the fellas was getting in time. And then on the weekends, they'd always go around and serenade, like for instance, I remember you always tell me about like St. Charles Street. They'd go around, had different people that'd go around and serenade and pick up money. And then they'd come down the Irish Channel. My daddy was born and raised out there in the Irish Channel. In fact, he had some cousins that still lives on Phillip Street. That's about between Annunciation and Laura or something like that. And from when I was told, the house that they lived in was the house that my daddy's mother and father once owned. Then there was another house that he had one time that he owned, but he lost that to his half-sister one time. And then after, when he got mad, he always said, well, the children started coming so fast, he had to give up music, so he had to go get him a job. So with the Stella and all, he would play at some time on weekends, and he always told me how he met my mother. My mother's originally from Donaldsonville, Louisiana. Well, Donaldsonville, Louisiana is the home of the Claiborne. That was one of the great teacher and brass band, dance band. They had for Louisiana. And I remember a kid very well. Where we lived on the street was about a half a block from one of the man's street called a railroad. Then they had a school, and in the back of the school was a square. And in the back of that was the courthouse. And in that square, they had what they call a pavilion. I remember every Sunday, this band, Claiborne band, seemed like it was hired through the city to play a concert. And they had whites in the color all around in the park. We'd listen to that, and the band was dressed up in very nice uniform. They looked very nice, and it was built in a circle like, you know. And the leader, Claiborne would be up in the center directing, you know, the band with his baton and everything. They played, well, they did mostly reading. Everything was read, and they played marches and a lot of pop tunes that were popular at that time for brass bands, see.
